expectations.text: Output warns that aggregating to a static graph loses temporal information and conflates different time periods
expectations.evidence: response.md opens: 'collapsing 3 years of timestamped interactions into a single weighted adjacency matrix destroys the temporal structure that carries most of the substantive information in an email dataset.' A dedicated section 'What you lose by aggregating' enumerates three losses: causal ordering, burstiness/inter-event times, and recurrence vs. one-shot. The three-year span across different periods is implicitly addressed via the burstiness point (crisis week vs. even spread) and explicitly via the snapshot-panel option.

expectations.text: Output mentions time-respecting paths (temporal paths that respect arrow of time) as a key concept
expectations.evidence: response.md section header 'Causal ordering (time-respecting paths)' and body: 'a time-respecting path from i to j is a sequence of contacts at times t₁ < t₂ < ... < tₖ. Static analysis ignores this ordering.' The concept is also tied to the quantitative consequence (30–70% lower reachability) and the betweenness caveat table.

expectations.text: Output recommends temporal network analysis tools (pathpy, teneto, snap-temporal, or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: response.md Option C: 'Compute temporal betweenness and temporal closeness using teneto (Python) or pathpy.' Both tools are named, and working teneto code is provided with import and API call demonstrating TemporalNetwork construction, temporal_closeness_centrality, and temporal_betweenness_centrality.

expectations.text: Output explains the difference between metrics on the static aggregate vs. metrics on the temporal network
expectations.evidence: response.md 'The betweenness caveat': 'static betweenness on the aggregate counts all paths. Temporal betweenness counts only time-respecting shortest paths. These can produce qualitatively different rankings.' The 'key communicators' table explicitly marks each metric with 'Works on aggregate? Yes / Partially / No' to distinguish static-safe metrics from temporal-only ones.

expectations.text: Output does NOT simply validate the static-aggregation plan as sufficient for understanding communication dynamics
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly calls the plan out in the first paragraph: 'has a critical flaw for several of the questions you likely care about.' The dedicated section 'The one mistake to avoid right now' warns against reporting static betweenness as information brokerage. Three tiered options are offered, with Option C (full temporal) marked 'best.' The aggregate is positioned as a baseline, not as sufficient.

claims.claim: The skill triggered on the temporal network classification axis
claims.evidence: response.md classifies the network on seven axes and explicitly flags the Time axis as 'Continuous-time event sequence — this is the critical one,' consistent with the transcript's description of the skill trigger.

claims.claim: Temporal reachability is 30–70% lower than static reachability (attributed to Holme & Saramäki 2012)
claims.evidence: The statistic appears in response.md and the reference is listed. The figure is consistent with the finding reported in Holme & Saramäki (2012) 'Temporal networks,' Physics Reports 519:97–125, which documents substantially reduced reachability in temporal networks compared to their static projections.

claims.claim: Static betweenness and temporal betweenness can produce qualitatively different rankings
claims.evidence: response.md states this directly and gives a concrete directional example (node that emails group A before B but not the reverse).

claims.claim: teneto API call shown uses temporal_closeness_centrality and temporal_betweenness_centrality
claims.evidence: Code in response.md Option C shows exactly these two calls. These are valid teneto networkmeasures functions.

claims.claim: Response recommends monthly windows (36 snapshots) for Option B
claims.evidence: response.md Option B: 'Window choice: use monthly windows for a 3-year dataset (36 snapshots). Check sensitivity against weekly and quarterly.' This is a reasonable default for a 3-year, 2.3M-event dataset.

suggestions.reason: Expectation 1 ('loses temporal information and conflates different time periods') is partially satisfied by any response that mentions aggregation has limits. A sharper version would require the output to explain a *specific* consequence — e.g., that paths counted in the aggregate may be causally impossible — rather than just noting information loss. The current assertion passed on strong evidence, but a weaker response could also pass by merely saying 'aggregation loses some detail.'

No assertion checks whether the output correctly explains *why* temporal betweenness differs from static betweenness (the causal-ordering / time-respecting-path mechanism). The output did explain this well, but since no assertion required it, a response that only named the tools and said 'metrics differ' would also pass expectations 3 and 4.

No assertion checks whether the output provides actionable next steps or code. The output did include working NetworkX and teneto code, which is a meaningful quality signal that none of the assertions capture.

eval_feedback.overall: All five assertions are well-targeted and were genuinely satisfied by the output. The main gap is that assertions 1 and 4 could be strengthened to require mechanistic explanation (not just presence of the concept) to discriminate a superficial response from a substantive one.
